email.resetBody:
Hi {name},

Someone asked to reset the password for your Backup Hub account. To choose a new one, open this link:

{link}

It works once and expires in {minutes} minutes. Resetting also lifts a sign-in lockout.

If this wasn't you, ignore this email — your password stays as it is.
email.changedSubject: Your Backup Hub password was changed
email.changedBody:
Hi {name},

The password for your Backup Hub account was just reset using an emailed link, and you've been signed out everywhere.

If this wasn't you, contact your Backup Hub admin straight away.

folderId.helpText: The long ID at the end of a Drive folder's URL. Leave blank to upload to the Drive root.

refreshToken.helpText: Obtained via Google's OAuth consent flow with the drive.file scope — see README.

folderPath.label: Folder path (optional)

clientSecret.label: Client secret (optional)

refreshToken.label: OAuth refresh token
refreshToken.helpText: Obtained via Microsoft's OAuth consent flow with the Files.ReadWrite and offline_access scopes — see README.

tenantId.label: Tenant ID
tenantId.helpText: "common" for personal Microsoft accounts, or your Azure AD tenant ID for work/school accounts.

to.label: Send to
to.helpText: Separate multiple addresses with commas. Independent of the task's notification recipients.

maxSizeMb.label: Maximum file size (MB)
maxSizeMb.helpText: Backups larger than this are skipped, not emailed — and the run history shows them as skipped. Check your mail provider's attachment limit (many cap around 25 MB, and email adds ~33% overhead).

pathPrefix.label: Remote folder (optional)
pathPrefix.helpText: Created if it doesn't exist. Start with "/" for an absolute path, otherwise it's relative to the login folder.

implicitTls.label: Use implicit TLS
implicitTls.helpText: Only for older servers that expect TLS from the start (usually port 990). Most servers use explicit TLS — leave unchecked.

allowSelfSigned.label: Allow self-signed / untrusted certificates
allowSelfSigned.helpText: The connection is still encrypted, but the server's identity isn't verified.

pathPrefix.label: Remote folder (optional)
pathPrefix.helpText: Created if it doesn't exist. Start with "/" for an absolute path, otherwise it's relative to the login folder.

password.label: Password
password.helpText: Leave blank if you're using a private key.

privateKey.label: Private key (optional)
privateKey.helpText: Paste the full key in OpenSSH or PEM format. Stored encrypted.

-----END OPENSSH PRIVATE KEY-----

hostFingerprint.label: Server host key fingerprint (recommended)
hostFingerprint.helpText: Click "Test connection" to see the server's fingerprint. Once set, connections to a server with a different key are refused.

pathPrefix.label: Remote folder (optional)
pathPrefix.helpText: Created if it doesn't exist. Start with "/" for an absolute path, otherwise it's relative to the user's home folder.

users.title: Users
users.intro: Admins manage users and system notifications. Backup tasks are private to their owner: admins can see how many tasks a user has, but not the tasks themselves unless the owner shares them. Deleting a user also deletes all of their tasks and backups.

compatibility.mysql: Also MySQL-compatible services such as Amazon RDS / Aurora MySQL, PlanetScale and TiDB.
compatibility.postgres: Also Postgres-compatible services such as Supabase, Neon, Amazon RDS / Aurora PostgreSQL and TimescaleDB.
compatibility.mongodb: Self-hosted MongoDB and MongoDB Atlas — for Atlas, enter the cluster's host (e.g. cluster0.abcde.mongodb.net); it connects with TLS automatically.

locationsPage.title: Save locations
locationsPage.intro: Off-site places your backups get copied to. Saved locations can be used by any of your tasks — enter the credentials once, pick them from a task's page, and changing them here updates every task that uses them. Task-only locations belong to a single task and can't be used anywhere else. Nobody else, admins included, can see these.
locationsPage.noSaved: No saved locations yet — add one, or make a task-only location reusable.
locationsPage.taskOnlyDescription: Tied to one of your tasks. Locations someone you shared a task with added are listed too: you can remove them, but only they can change their credentials.
locationsPage.editIntroTaskOnly: {provider} · task-only. Changes apply to the task using it from the next backup on.
locationsPage.editIntroSaved: {provider} · saved location. Changes apply to every task using it from the next backup on.

channelsPage.title: Notifications
channelsPage.intro: Your notification channels: where your tasks send backup success/failure alerts — email, ntfy, Telegram or Discord. Saved channels can be used by any of your tasks: set them up once, pick them from a task's page, and changing them here updates every task that uses them. Task-only channels belong to a single task. Nobody else, admins included, can see these.
channelsPage.noSaved: No saved channels yet — add one, or make a task-only channel reusable.
channelsPage.taskOnlyDescription: Tied to one of your tasks. Channels someone you shared a task with added are listed too: you can remove them, but only they can change their settings.
channelsPage.editIntroTaskOnly: {type} · task-only. Changes apply to the task using it.
channelsPage.editIntroSaved: {type} · saved channel. Changes apply to every task using it.

systemPage.title: System notifications
systemPage.intro: Server-wide alerts for account and task-lifecycle events (email, ntfy, Telegram or Discord), managed by admins. Backup success/failure alerts are separate: each user sets those up under <link>Notifications</link> and on each task's page.
systemPage.recipientsDescription: Who is alerted about account and task-lifecycle events, and for which ones.

apiKeysPage.title: API keys
apiKeysPage.intro: Used by external apps to call the REST API at /api/v1/*. Each key carries its own scopes and can be pinned to a single task. A key acts as you: it can never do more on a task than you can, and it stops working on a task if that task is unshared from you.
apiKeysPage.keysDescription: Revoke a key as soon as the app using it no longer needs access.
